item.title: Nevada wildfire leaves six injured, thousands forced to evacuate: Here's why fires are surging across the US
item.description: A fast-spreading wildfire northwest of Reno, Nevada, has injured at least six people and forced thousands to evacuate. The Hawk Fire has burned over 13,000 acres, as dry conditions fuel rising wildfire activity across the US, with over 50,000 fires recorded in 2026.
item.dc:creator: Swati Gandhi
item.content:encoded: At least six people have been injured, and thousands of others have been forced to evacuate after a fast-spreading wildfire broke out northwest of Reno, Nevada.Here's what we know about the Hawk FireThe Hawk Fire started on the morning of 22 August and spread rapidly to more than 23 square miles (60 sq km) by 23 August across the Peavine Peak area of the Humboldt–Toiyabe National Forest, where homes and businesses are located near the California state line. There was zero containment, AP reported. At least three first responders and three civilians were reported injured.US Forest Service incident commander Shane Ackerson told reporters on Sunday (23 August) that the blaze was “human-caused” and added that, as of 2 PM on Sunday (New York time), more than 13,000 acres (5,261 hectares) of land had been burned, with an unknown number of structures destroyed, Bloomberg reported. Roughly 90,000 residents in the region have been impacted by the fire, with at least 42,000 ordered to evacuate as the “GO NOW” zone expanded to the edge of the University of Nevada. Another 45,000 people were in the adjacent evacuation warning zone. Authorities urged residents to be prepared to stay away for several days, as shifting and strengthening winds were expected to make the fire even more unpredictable. Over 1,000 first responders, including some 800 fire personnel, were working to contain the blaze.On Sunday (local time), roughly 10,000 people were left without power in Washoe County, down from 60,000 on Saturday (22 August). Additionally, portions of US Route 395, a major north-south highway, were also closed due to the fire. Reno, which has a population of more than 280,000, is Nevada’s largest city outside the Las Vegas metropolitan area.Nevada Governor declares state of emergencyNevada Governor Joe Lombardo declared a state of emergency in Washoe County and called in the Nevada National Guard, including two helicopter crews for aerial firefighting and 60 troops to assist police in protecting evacuated neighbourhoods. Around 800 firefighters were also deployed to tackle the blaze.In a statement posted on social media late at night on 22 August, Reno Mayor Hillary Schieve said, "If you have been told to evacuate, please don't wait!" and added, "Structures have already been burned in this fire, and your life is more important than a building. Evacuating before the fire arrives also allows our firefighters to focus their efforts on battling the blaze."Why are wildfires spreading across the US?The growing wildfire activity has raised concerns about the increasingly dry and volatile conditions fuelling fires across the US.Wildfire season in the US generally runs from May through November, with activity usually peaking during the summer, according to the Western Fire Chiefs Association (WFCA). In the early 1950s, the season lasted roughly five months. However, it has expanded to about 7 months amid climate change, with deteriorating weather conditions increasing the risk of wildfires. Hot, dry weather creates the conditions most conducive to wildfires.In the Midwest, wetter conditions during winter and spring, including greater rainfall and snowfall, generally limit fire activity. In Northern California, the wetter fall and winter months mean wildfires are more common during spring and summer. August is typically the busiest month for wildfires as temperatures rise and conditions become increasingly dry. States that frequently report high numbers of wildfires include California, Georgia, Texas, North Carolina, Florida, Arizona and Oklahoma.Earlier this month, three wildfires north of Reno, driven by hot, dry and windy weather, forced more than 13,000 people to leave their homes, according to the Nevada National Guard. Nevada also saw 15 new fires break out on 22 August alone. Months of dry weather, along with record-low snowfall across the American West during the past winter, have created conditions favourable for wildfires.Over 50,000 wildfires have been reported in 2026 so farAccording to the National Interagency Fire Centre, firefighters across the United States have responded to 50,580 wildfires that have burned more than 7.7 million acres, 129 per cent of the 10-year average for fires and 169 per cent for acres burned. On 22 August, 200 new fires were reported nationwide, including five new large fires, with firefighters working to contain 79 large fires and 22,122 firefighters and support personnel assigned to incidents nationwide.According to the official data, the Northwest continues to have the most fire activity in the nation, with 29 large fires and 11 complex incident management teams assigned. All 10 geographic areas currently list at least one large fire.This arrangement avoids jumping back and forth between the local fire and the national wildfire situation. It first finishes the Hawk Fire and the official response, then explains the broader conditions, and finally gives the national statistics.(with agency inputs)

item.title: Nehru told Queen Elizabeth ‘India will always be on the side of Russia’: Ex-UK PM Boris Johnson
item.description: Speaking at The Economic Times 'World Leaders Forum', Ex-UK PM Boris Johnson said he once told Queen Elizabeth II about “how difficult it was to persuade our Indian friends to firmly come down against Russia.”
item.dc:creator: Akriti Anand
item.content:encoded: The United Kingdom's former Prime Minister Boris Johnson made a striking remark about the India-Russia relationship on Saturday, recalling a conversation with the late Queen Elizabeth on the matter.Speaking at The Economic Times 'World Leaders Forum', Johnson said he once told Queen Elizabeth II about "how difficult it was to persuade our Indian friends to firmly come down against Russia."He then went on to share the late queen's response, in which she recalled her meeting with India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, in 1952.The Queen told Johnson that in 1952, when she met PM Nehru, he said that "India will always be on the side of Russia.""Oh yes, I remember, in 1952, when I was talking to Prime Minister Nehru, he [Nehru] said, 'Your Majesty, India will always basically be on the side of Russia," said Johnson, recalling his conversation with the Queen."Somethings never change. They just are," ex-UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson said, adding that he was "very struck" by that "analysis.""I don't know whether you agree with that analysis, but I was very struck by that. And, you know, I think we have to go with the historical reality," Johnson added.Johnson said he had this conversation with Queen Elizabeth II shortly before her death in 2022. Elizabeth II was Queen of the United Kingdom and other Commonwealth realms from February 6, 1952, until she died in 2022.At the summit, Johnson spoke at length about the protracted Russia-Ukraine war, the Strait of Hormuz crisis, India-UK ties and UK domestic politics, among other issues.The former UK Prime Minister's statement came amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war. Russia launched what it called a "special military operation," against Ukraine in 2022.Britain has been one of Ukraine's strongest supporters since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, providing military support, economic aid and diplomatic backing.UK's Burnham to visit UkraineUK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will visit Ukraine on Monday on his first overseas trip since taking office, and will announce British support to help Kyiv improve its domestic production of long-range missiles.Burnham will be in Ukraine to co-chair a meeting of the so-called Coalition of the Willing, a group of countries backing Ukraine, on Monday when he is also due to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Reuters reported.He is set to announce that Britain has agreed to allow European missile manufacturer MBDA to release classified information on British-made components used in the SCALP long-range cruise missile, according to his office.That will help enable France and Ukraine to establish local assembly lines for the missile, which shares British and French technology, according to Downing Street."Ukraine's security is our security," Burnham said in a statement, adding that Britain would stand by Ukraine "for as long as it takes".
